newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower in quiet trade.

text.p: The Paris bourse, shrugging off Wall Street's rise to a fresh record, opened lower on Friday in a consolidation of its recent gains, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.75 points, or 0.16 percent, at 2,932.23 at 0925 GMT. The CAC-40 July futures contract was down six at 2,935.

Canal Plus shares rose 2.46 percent after the pay TV group said on Friday that it expected to generate a profit of three billion francs on two transactions with the Kirch Group. It will sell its 37.5 percent stake in Germany's Premiere to Kirch and buy Kirch's 45 percent stake in Telepiu of Italy.
As a result Canal Plus, which had expected to break even in 1997, now expects a three billion franc profit for the year.

Defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF's stock was up 4.54 percent at 170.40 francs, bolstered by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's comments on Thursday evening that the government would be "flexible" and "not ideological" as far as privatisations were concerned.
Lockheed Martin's plan to take over Northrop Grumman turns up the pressure on Europeans to form competitive defence giants.
Car parts manufacturer Valeo also rose against the grain, adding 2.84 percent after reporting a 14.6 percent rise in first-half sales and forecasting higher results.
